Induction Training plays a very important role in preparing entrants in the company to fulfill their responsibilities.
The given manual aims at supporting the entity based on specific policies and system for learning and engagement of new employees, according to the responsibilities and work nature of each authority. Included in the guide are the vision, mission and objectives of the entity along with the organizational structure, alternative modes of operation, and step-by-step procedures for system access.
The mission of Gautam Solar Private Limited is to be the leading solar energy solution provider in terms of quality, efficiency, and innovation by managing our partners, customers, and associates in a productive and sustainable manner.
Our vision is to accelerate the global transition to clean energy by delivering high-performance, reliable solar products while upholding the highest standards of ethics, human rights, and environmental stewardship.
Gautam Solar Private Limited has over a decade of experience in manufacturing and marketing a diverse range of solar products, including high-efficiency solar modules, solar panels, and solar solutions for residential, commercial, and industrial applications. The company's continued commitment to customer-oriented approach and quality control measures have enabled us to offer reliable, sustainable solar energy solutions to many satisfied customers across India and internationally.

chapters.title: Training & Awareness
chapters.text:
- All employees receive annual awareness training on:
- Recognising signs of stress (in self and colleagues).
- Available support channels.
- Reducing stigma around mental health.
- Managers & supervisors receive additional training on:
- Identifying team stress indicators.
- Conducting supportive conversations.
- Referring employees to EAP / HR without judgement.
- Quarterly wellbeing campaigns (e.g., “Stress-Free September”, mindfulness sessions).
## Intervention Procedures – When Stress or Mental Health Issues Arise
[table]
| Step | Action | Timeline |
| 1. Self-reporting or manager observation | Employee or manager reports concern to HR or EAP (confidential). No disciplinary | Immediate |
| 2. Initial assessment | EAP counsellor or HR conducts confidential assessment (severity, work-related fa | Within 48 hours |
| 3. Support plan | Recommendations may include: temporary workload reduction, job modification, ref | Within 5 working days |
| 4. Workplace adjustments | Manager implements agreed adjustments (e.g., flexible hours, reduced targets, te | Within 7 working days |
| 5. Follow-up | HR/EAP checks in with employee at 2, 4, and 8 weeks. Adjustments extended or mod | Ongoing |
## Confidentiality & Non-Discrimination
- All mental health disclosures are treated as strictly confidential (except where legally required to prevent harm).
- No employee shall face discrimination, demotion, or dismissal for seeking mental health support.
- Mental health conditions are treated like any other medical condition under the Company’s leave and accommodation policies.
## Return-to-Work Support
After absence due to mental health reasons, the Company provides a phased return-to-work plan (e.g., reduced hours initially, gradual increase). A return-to-work meeting is held with HR, the employee, and their supervisor to ensure a smooth transition.
## Hazardous Substance Control & Exposure Prevention
Gautam Solar Private Limited is committed to protecting employees from the health risks associated with exposure to hazardous substances used in solar module manufacturing. These include fluxes, soldering pastes, potting compounds (silicon / epoxy), cleaning solvents (isopropyl alcohol), adhesives, and other chemicals. The Company implements a hierarchy of controls – elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, and personal protective equipment (PPE) – to prevent or minimise exposure.
## Identification of Hazardous Substances
The Company maintains a chemical inventory and Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all hazardous substances used in the workplace. SDS are readily accessible to all employees in both English and local language (Hindi) at designated points (e.g., chemical storage area, production floor notice board).
Key hazardous substances in solar manufacturing include:
[table]
| Substance | Use | Health Hazard |
| Flux (rosin-based / no-clean) | Soldering (stringing) | Respiratory irritation, skin sensitisation |
| Isopropyl alcohol (IPA) | Cleaning cells, modules | Eye irritation, drowsiness, flammable |
| Potting compound (silicon / epoxy) | Junction box sealing | Skin/eye irritation, sensitisation |
| Silicone sealant | Framing | Eye irritation, fumes during curing |
| Solder fumes | Stringing | Metal fume fever, respiratory irritation |
| EVA (ethylene-vinyl acetate) | Lamination | Fumes during heating – respiratory irritant |
## Hierarchy of Controls – Active Measures
[table]
| Control Level | Examples at Gautam Solar |
| Elimination | Where possible, use mechanical / automated processes (e.g., automatic flux appli |
| Substitution | Use low-flux or no-clean flux with lower volatile organic compounds (VOCs); wate |
| Engineering Controls | Local exhaust ventilation (LEV) / fume extraction at soldering stations; enclose |
| Administrative Controls | Job rotation to reduce duration of exposure; restricted access to chemical stora |
| Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) | Provided as per SDS and risk assessment (see table below). |
## Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Matrix
[table]
| Task | Required PPE |
| Handling flux, IPA, potting compound | Nitrile gloves, chemical-resistant apron, safety goggles |
| Soldering (stringing) | Fume extraction + safety glasses + (optional) respirator if LEV inadequate |
| Potting (junction box) | Nitrile gloves, safety goggles, face shield (for splashes) |
| Cleaning modules with IPA | Nitrile gloves, safety goggles, adequate ventilation |
| Laminator maintenance (hot EVA fumes) | Heat-resistant gloves + respirator with organic vapour cartridge |
| General chemical storage / dispensing | Gloves, goggles, apron + closed-toe shoes |
All PPE is provided free of cost. Employees must inspect PPE before use and report damage immediately.
## Exposure Monitoring & Health Surveillance
- Air monitoring for VOCs, solder fumes, and particulates is conducted annually (or more frequently if process changes) in high-risk areas (stringing, potting, laminator zone).

chapters.title: Overtime Compensation – All Forms of Excess Hours
chapters.text:
Gautam Solar Private Limited ensures that every hour worked beyond the employee’s contractual working hours is recorded and compensated as overtime. This applies regardless of whether the excess hours occur on a regular working day, a rest day, a public holiday, or outside the physical workplace (e.g., approved work from home). No employee is required to work overtime without consent, and no employee shall work for free.
## Definition of Overtime – What Counts as Excess Hours
Overtime includes any work performed:
- Beyond the daily working hours (e.g., after 6:00 PM on a normal day).
- Before the scheduled start time (e.g., starting at 8:00 AM instead of 9:00 AM without prior adjustment).
- On weekly rest days (the day off – typically Sunday or as per roster).
- On public holidays (national or declared company holidays).
- During meal breaks (if the employee is required to work through lunch/tea break).
- Outside the workplace (e.g., approved remote work, business travel, attending calls/emails after hours, if such work is directed or expected by the supervisor).
## What Does NOT Count as Overtime
- Voluntary, unauthorised extension of work without supervisor approval.
- Time spent on personal activities during work hours.
- Travel to and from the workplace (unless the employee is called in specifically for an emergency).
## Approval Process
- Overtime requires prior written approval from the department head (except in genuine emergencies where after-event approval is obtained within 48 hours).
- Unauthorised overtime is not compensated and may lead to disciplinary action if repeated.
[table]
|  | Compensation Rate |
| On a normal working day (beyond 8 hours) | Double the ordinary hourly wage (as per Factories Act) |
| On a weekly rest day | Double the ordinary hourly wage |
| On a public holiday | Double the ordinary hourly wage |
| During meal break (if required to work) | Double the ordinary hourly wage for the break period |
| Remote / after-hours work (approved) | Same as above – calculated based on total logged hours |
- Hourly wage calculation = (Basic + DA) ÷ 26 ÷ 8 (or as per applicable law). Overtime rate = 2 × ordinary hourly wage.
## Recording of All Excess Hours
- The biometric attendance system captures early arrivals and late departures.
- For remote work or after-hours work not captured by biometric, employees must log hours in a digital timesheet approved by their supervisor.
- All recorded overtime hours are reflected in the monthly working hour report and payroll.
## Payment of Overtime
- Overtime payments are made along with the regular monthly salary.
- The payslip clearly shows the number of overtime hours and the amount paid.
- Overtime is not converted into compensatory time off unless the employee specifically requests and the Company agrees in writing (legal requirement is payment – time-off is optional extra).
## Limits on Overtime
- As per the Factories Act, overtime is voluntary (no employee can be forced).
- Maximum overtime: 12 hours per week.
- Total working hours including overtime: max 60 hours per week (as per law).
- The Company monitors overtime through the time-tracking system and alerts supervisors when limits are approached.
## Consequences of Non-Compliance
- Employees who work unauthorised overtime will not be compensated, and may receive a warning.
- Supervisors who encourage or expect unpaid overtime may face disciplinary action, including compensation recovery for affected employees.
## Employee Responsibility
- Obtain approval before working overtime.
- Record your hours accurately – do not under-report or over-report.
- Report any case where you are asked to work without proper compensation to HR or the whistleblower channel.
## Communication of Remuneration System to Employees
Gautam Solar Private Limited ensures that every employee understands their remuneration – including base salary, bonus schemes, financial benefits, and salary advancement opportunities. Communication is not limited to HR personnel; supervisors, written documents, and digital tools also play a role.
## Initial Communication (Onboarding)
- During induction, each new employee receives a written compensation statement (in English or local language as applicable) explaining:
- Base salary (basic pay, allowances, deductions).
- Eligibility for overtime, bonus, and other variable pay.
- Statutory and company benefits (PF, ESI, gratuity, medical insurance, leave encashment).
- Salary advancement criteria (how to move to higher pay grades).
- The employee’s reporting manager also explains the compensation structure in a one-on-one meeting.
## Salary Grid / Matrix (Available for All Employees)
- The Company maintains a transparent salary grid that shows:
- Pay grades / levels (e.g., Level 1 to Level 10).
- Minimum and maximum salary for each grade.
- Criteria for moving between grades (tenure, performance rating, skill acquisition).

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangements (For Eligible Roles)
chapters.text:
- Flexible start/end times: Employees in administrative, sales, or support roles may, with manager approval, adjust their start and end times within a core window (e.g., 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM) to accommodate school drop-off/pick-up.
- Compressed work week: Where operationally feasible, employees may work longer hours for fewer days (e.g., 10 hours for 4 days) to have an extra day off.
- Work from home: Up to 2 days per week for eligible roles (subject to manager approval and IT security compliance).
- These arrangements are reviewed every 6 months and can be revoked if business needs require, but with at least 2 weeks’ notice.
## Part-Time & Job-Share Options
- Employees returning from parental leave may request part-time work (reduced hours) for up to 1 year after their return, with pro-rated salary and benefits.
- Job-sharing (two employees sharing one full-time role) is available for certain positions; the Company will facilitate matching of candidates.
## Breastfeeding Support
- A clean, private lactation room (with refrigerator for milk storage) is available at the manufacturing facility and office.
- Nursing mothers are allowed two paid nursing breaks of 30 minutes each per day (in addition to regular breaks) for up to 1 year after childbirth.
## Employee Assistance for Elder Care
- Elder care referral service: The Company partners with a third-party provider to help employees find reliable elder care services (home care, day centres, nursing homes).
- Flexible leave for elder care: Employees caring for elderly parents may request unpaid leave of absence (up to 3 months) or reduced working hours, without losing seniority.
## Financial Counseling & Family Support
- Financial literacy workshops (budgeting, saving, child education planning) are offered quarterly.
- Employees can access subsidised legal advice for family matters (will, inheritance, adoption) through the Company’s empanelled legal firm.
## Communication & Awareness
- All work-life balance initiatives are explained during induction and summarised on the company intranet.
- Posters and handouts in Hindi and English are displayed on notice boards.
- Employees can raise suggestions for additional family-friendly measures through the suggestion box or HR.
## Flexible Working Arrangements
Gautam Solar Private Limited offers a range of flexible working arrangements to help all employees balance their home and work lives. These options are available to eligible employees regardless of gender, parental status, or role, subject to operational feasibility and manager approval. The Company believes that flexibility improves productivity, reduces stress, and increases loyalty.
## Types of Flexible Working Arrangements
[table]
| Arrangement | Description | Eligibility (Indicative) |
| Flexi-time | Employees choose their start and end times within a core window (e.g., 10:00 AM  | Office, sales, design, and administrative roles. |
| Compressed work week | Work longer hours on fewer days (e.g., 10 hours for 4 days) to get an extra day  | Roles where continuous presence is not required daily. |
| Telecommuting / Work from home | Work from home partially (e.g., 1-3 days per week) or fully (subject to role). E | Roles that do not require physical presence (design, admin, sales, planning). |
| Part-time work | Work less than standard full-time hours (e.g., 20–30 hours/week) with pro-rated  | Any role that can be scaled down; manager approval required. |
| Job-sharing | Two employees share the responsibilities of one full-time role, each working par | Suitable for roles with divisible tasks; the Company may facilitate matching. |
| Variable / annualised hours | Work hours vary across weeks or months (e.g., more in busy season, less in lean  | Production planning, maintenance, seasonal support roles. |
| Phased retirement | Employees nearing retirement age reduce their working hours gradually (e.g., 4 d | Employees aged 55+ with minimum 10 years of service. |
## Eligibility & Approval Process
- All regular employees (permanent, full-time) may request any of the above arrangements, subject to:
- Role suitability (some production roles may not permit telecommuting or job-sharing).
- Manager approval based on business continuity.
- No adverse impact on team performance or customer service.
## Request process:
- Employee submits written request to their reporting manager (and HR).
- Manager evaluates within 7 working days, consulting with team and HR.
- If approved, a trial period of 3 months applies (except for part-time or job-share).
- After trial, arrangement may be made permanent or modified.
- Denials must be in writing with clear business reasons.
## Telecommuting / Work from Home (WFH) – Specific Provisions
- Eligible roles: Those that do not require physical presence on the factory floor (e.g., sales coordination, procurement, HR administration, finance, design, customer support).

chapters.title: Transparency & Employee Communication
chapters.text:
- Once every two years, the Company publishes an internal summary (anonymised) on the notice board / intranet stating:
- That a pay equity audit has been completed
- The overall pay gap (e.g., gender pay gap as a percentage)
- Key actions taken (e.g., "adjusted salaries for X employees in Y department")
- No individual employee data is disclosed.
- Employees may request anonymised aggregate information about pay equity through HR.
## Grievance Mechanism for Pay Discrimination
- Any employee who believes they are paid less than a colleague for equal work (considering legitimate factors) may raise a complaint through HR or the Grievance Committee.
- The complaint is investigated within 15 working days. If discrimination is found, the employee receives back pay and the practice is corrected.
## Continuous Improvement
- The Company tracks the effectiveness of corrective actions by comparing pay gaps in subsequent audits.
- External benchmarking (industry salary surveys) is used to ensure the Company’s pay practices remain competitive and fair.
## nternal Mobility Policy
Gautam Solar Private Limited encourages employees to grow their careers within the Company. Internal mobility allows employees to take on new challenges, develop skills, and progress without leaving the organisation. The Company supports four types of mobility: vertical, horizontal, geographical, and transversal.
## Vertical Mobility (Promotions / Upward Movement)
- Employees advance to the next level in the organisational hierarchy (e.g., from Officer to Senior Officer, from Manager to Senior Manager).
## Process:
- Open positions are advertised internally before external recruitment.
- Eligible employees apply through HR.
- Selection is based on performance (last 2 appraisal ratings), tenure (minimum 1 year in
- current role), and a competency assessment.
- Promotions are effective from the date of approval, with revised salary and benefits.
- Target: Approximately 15-20 promotions per year across all departments.
## Horizontal Mobility (Lateral Transfer / Same Level, Different Function)
- Employees move to a different department or role at the same job level (e.g., from Quality Control to Production, from Sales to Marketing).
## Process:
- Internal job postings are published quarterly.
- Employees may apply with endorsement from their current manager.
- A trial period of 2-3 months may apply to assess fit.
- Benefits: Broadens experience, prevents monotony, and builds cross-functional understanding.
- Target: Approximately 10-15 horizontal transfers per year.
## Geographical Mobility (Different Site / Location)
- Employees relocate to another company site (e.g., from Delhi headquarters to a new manufacturing plant in another state) either at the same level or with promotion.
## Support provided:
- Relocation allowance (one-time payment equal to one month’s basic salary).
- Temporary housing assistance for up to 30 days.
- Travel expenses for the employee and family (if permanent transfer).
- For cross-site learning assignments (short-term, up to 6 months): accommodation and daily allowance.
- Process: Employees express interest through HR when a new site opens or a position becomes available. Selection based on skills and willingness.
## Transversal Mobility (Cross-Skilling / Moving Across Different Roles)
- Employees develop transferable skills and move into roles that are not directly hierarchical or lateral but leverage newly acquired competencies (e.g., from Production to Maintenance, from HR to Compliance, from Accounts to Procurement).
## Programs to enable transversal mobility:
- Skill Inventory & Gap Analysis: HR maintains a skill inventory for each employee. Every 2 years, a gap analysis identifies potential cross-skilling opportunities.
- Job Rotation Program (3-6 months): Employees work in a different function to learn new skills while backfilling vacancies or covering leaves.
- Cross-Functional Projects: Employees may join temporary project teams (e.g., new plant setup, digitalisation, safety improvement) outside their regular role.
- Mentorship & Shadowing: Employees can shadow a colleague in another department for up to 10 hours per month with manager approval.
- Internal Certification: The Company offers short courses (online or in-person) on topics such as solar cell technology, quality systems, supply chain management, and business communication.
- Eligibility: Employees with minimum 2 years of service and consistent performance rating of “Meets Expectations” or higher.
## General Provisions for All Internal Mobility
- Communication: All internal vacancies are posted on notice boards and the company intranet. Employees are encouraged to self-nominate.
- Manager Support: Managers must not block reasonable transfer requests unless business continuity would be seriously harmed. Denials must be in writing with justification.

chapters.title: Grievance Mechanism
chapters.text:
## Reporting Channels
- Gautam Solar Private Limited offers multiple confidential reporting channels for employees to raise grievances or report incidents. These channels include:
- Dedicated Hotline: [Insert phone number]
- Confidential Email: grievance@gautamsolar.com
- Grievance Boxes located in common areas for anonymous submissions.
- Online Platform: [Insert URL, e.g., www.gautamsolar.com/grievance]
## Types of Grievances Covered
- The mechanism covers grievances related to:
- Discrimination based on gender, race, religion, ethnicity, disability, or any other characteristic.
- Harassment, including physical, verbal, sexual, or psychological abuse.
- Child labor violations or risk of exploitation.
- Forced labor and human trafficking incidents.
- Unsafe working conditions.
- Breach of labor rights including wage theft or unlawful termination.
## Grievance Submission Process
- Employees can submit grievances confidentially through the reporting channels.
- Reports should include as much detail as possible, such as the nature of the grievance, individuals involved, dates, and any evidence.
- Anonymous submissions are accepted, and whistleblowers are protected from retaliation.
## nvestigation Process
- Upon receipt of a grievance, the Grievance Committee or HR department initiates an investigation. Investigations are handled by trained personnel to ensure impartiality.
- Initial response is provided within 5 working days and investigations are typically concluded within 15 working days.
- Relevant parties are interviewed, and evidence is reviewed to determine the appropriate course of action.
## Non-Retaliation Policy
- Gautam Solar maintains a strict non-retaliation policy. Employees who report grievances are protected from any form of retaliation, including demotion, dismissal, or harassment.
- Disciplinary action will be taken against anyone found retaliating against whistleblowers.
## Appeal Process
- If the employee is dissatisfied with the outcome of the investigation, they can file an appeal with senior management.
- Appeals are reviewed by senior management or an independent third party, and further action is taken as necessary.

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure
chapters.text:
## Purpose and Scope
- The whistleblower procedure at Gautam Solar Private Limited aims to encourage employees to report unethical behavior, misconduct, or violations of company policies without fear of retaliation. This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and stakeholders.
## Confidential Reporting Channels
- Gautam Solar provides multiple confidential reporting channels for whistleblowers. Employees can report concerns through:
- A dedicated hotline: [Insert phone number]
- An email: whistleblower@gautamsolar.com
- A secure online platform:
[Insert URL, e.g., www.gautamsolar.com/whistleblower]
- All reports made through these channels will be treated with the highest confidentiality.
## Reporting Process
- Employees are encouraged to provide as much detail as possible regarding the misconduct, including dates, locations, individuals involved, and any evidence available.
- Reports can be made anonymously if preferred, but providing contact information may help in follow-up investigations.
## nvestigation Procedures
- Upon receiving a whistleblower report, Gautam Solar will initiate an internal investigation promptly.
- Investigations will be conducted by designated personnel trained in handling such matters.
- The investigation process will include interviewing relevant parties, gathering evidence, and ensuring that the whistleblower's identity is protected throughout the investigation.
## Non-Retaliation Policy
- Gautam Solar has a strict non-retaliation policy to protect whistleblowers from any form of retaliation, including harassment, discrimination, or punitive actions.
- Employees who report concerns in good faith will be shielded from retaliation, and any retaliatory actions will be subject to disciplinary measures.
## Follow-Up and Communication
- After the investigation is concluded, the whistleblower may receive a summary of the findings and any actions taken, unless disclosure could compromise confidentiality or legal requirements.
- Employees are encouraged to remain engaged and report any further issues related to the initial complaint.
